title: `-0.0` in arithmetic on the streaming engine: two zeros, literal shortcuts per morsel
verdict: IEEE: `1 / -0.0` is -inf; with a literal operand the sign depends on the morsel's length
description: Arithmetic keeps the sign of zero: `1.0 / -0.0` is -inf, `-(0.0)` and `0.0 * -1` are -0.0, `sqrt(-0.0)` is -0.0. Comparison, grouping and sorting are in polars-zero-order.

The streaming engine runs the in-memory kernels on each morsel. With a literal operand, a morsel of two rows or more takes the literal kernels' shortcuts: `x + 0.0` and `x - 0.0` return `x`, so `-0.0 + 0.0` and `-0.0 - (-0.0)` are -0.0, and `0.0 - x` is `-x`, so `0.0 - 0.0` is -0.0. A morsel of one row takes the IEEE operations (0.0 in those three cases).

Which rows land in a one-row morsel depends on the frame's size and the machine's thread count: on 10 cores every row of a frame of up to 10 rows did, so `-0.0 + 0.0` was 0.0 there and -0.0 in memory; from about 100 rows none did. The in-memory engine's behaviour is in polars-zero-sign.
polars-zero-add records the literal-shortcut part of this finding from #590's probe and is the id the engine tables cite.

notes: zero-sign-arith (`1 / z`, `-z`, `z * -1`, `sqrt` on -0.0 and 0.0) gives the same on both engines; for these the shortcuts and IEEE agree.

s-zero-sign-literal counts the negative zeros of `x + 0.0`, `x - (-0.0)`, `x - 0.0` and `0.0 - x` over x = -0.0, 0.0, … : on 6000 rows 3000 in each column on both engines (the shortcuts); on 4 rows in memory 2 in each (the shortcuts), streaming 0, 0, 2, 0 (IEEE).

A manual repro of `x + 0.0` on n copies of -0.0 under streaming gave IEEE's 0.0 in every row for n up to 10 and the shortcut's -0.0 in all rows from n = 100; between them one row of some sizes was 0.0 (n = 11: 10 of 11 rows -0.0). In memory every size gave -0.0. Streaming splits a small frame into several morsels on this 10-core machine, and a one-row morsel takes the column kernel, as for the scalar divisor (polars-double-scalar-divisor, PL-3).
`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` collects each `s-` observation's lazy query with `engine='in-memory'` and `engine='streaming'`. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

evidence.note: The literal kernels: `x + 0` and `x - 0` return `x`, `0 - x` is `-x`, `x * ±1` is `x` or `-x`.
Equal lengths take the array kernel, a length-1 side the scalar kernel.
The streaming engine evaluates each expression with polars-expr's `PhysicalExpr` on every morsel.

notes: Carried over from polars-zero-sign's round-2 reading; the morsel's length decides between the kernels, which the probe confirms. `impl_float_arith_kernel!` serves `f32` and `f64` alike, so the `Float32` rows rest on the source.
